story:
The Arawnite shamanesses of Snowdonia keep the old faith of the lord of the dead as the hill-folk kept it before the Church came up the valleys: not as worship, they say, but as manners, the courtesy a sensible people pays to the host whose house they will all one day sleep in. Saelonna is the eldest of them, and she has the book.

The Book of Arawn is the shamanesses' own: the names of the dead of the valleys, the roads they took, the debts they left, and the words the lord of the dead likes to hear. Saelonna reads it aloud in the middle valley, every day, slowly, from where she left off, and the dead of the valley lean in to listen as an old man leans toward a fire. The cyclopes the Followers pay stand round her while she reads. She does not need them. The dead would not let her come to harm before she finished.

Master Gerol of the Academy, who is too weak now to travel, says Morgana has taken an interest in the book, and in what the right words read to enough of the dead might raise. He wants it brought to Master Ferowl in Cotswold. Saelonna says the book was never Morgana's to want, and that Albion's wizards have never once asked to borrow it politely.
legend: Shaman Saelonna, level 46, in the middle valley of Snowdonia with half a dozen cyclopes (41) around her. She has no faction so the cyclopes do not come just because you hit her, but they are aggressive and close: clear them first. Plain melee in the data. Take her Book of Arawn to Master Ferowl in Cotswold for Symbol of the Broken.
